- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., Example 4, 5).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative or volatile (e.g., Example 1, 2).
- Lag in downward corrections: model often holds high prices longer than true market reacts (e.g., Example 3, 4).
- Overshoot after positive sentiment peaks — model tends to overreact and push prices too high (e.g., Example 5).
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows, fails to smoothly revert to historical mean (e.g., Example 1, 3).
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is high, model overestimates; when sentiment is low, model underestimates — adjust forecast slope based on sentiment trend (e.g., Example 2, 5).
